term.name: Polyalphabetic cipher
term.short: A polyalphabetic cipher switches among multiple substitution alphabets as it processes a message.
term.meta_title: Polyalphabetic Cipher — Definition and Analysis | CiphersOnline
term.meta_description: Learn how polyalphabetic ciphers select changing substitution alphabets, how Vigenère uses a keystream, and why repeated keys remain vulnerable.

body.title: Definition
body.html: A polyalphabetic cipher uses more than one substitution alphabet. A keystream selects the alphabet or shift for each position, so the same plaintext letter can encrypt to different ciphertext letters.

body.title: How it works
body.html: Vigenère repeats a keyword to form a keystream and applies the corresponding rows of a tabula recta. Autokey extends a short key with message material, while Beaufort changes the arithmetic relationship between key, plaintext, and ciphertext.

body.title: Cryptanalysis
body.html: Changing alphabets obscures the simple frequency profile of monoalphabetic substitution. A short repeating key, however, creates periodic structure: Kasiski examination and the index of coincidence can estimate its length, after which each position class can be analyzed separately.

faq.question: Is Vigenère a polyalphabetic cipher?
faq.answer: Yes. Each keystream letter selects a different shifted substitution alphabet.

faq.question: Does polyalphabetic mean secure?
faq.answer: No. Classical designs with repeated or predictable keystreams leak structure and are not suitable for modern protection.
